request.spec:
The header shows the signed-in user the due-totals of the people they watch, added up (0.00 when
watching no one).
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
The header shows the signed-in user the due-totals of the people they watch, added up (0.00 when
watching no one).

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
The header now shows a "Watched due total" figure for the signed-in user: the due-totals of the people they watch, added up. It shows 0.00 when they watch no one. All 4 acceptance tests pass in `bin/e2e`.

The change is only in the front end, in `src/main/frontend/src/app/features/people/people.ts`:
- A new `<strong data-testid="watched-due-total">` sits in the header, after "My reviews".
- A `watchedDueTotal` value works the figure out from the per-user watch list and each person's due-total, both of which the screen already loads. The server and stored data already had everything needed, so neither changed.
- A watched person whose due-total shows n/a is left out of the sum. That follows the existing crew due-total, since the request doesn't say what to do with them.

No audit records are written for this, and the test doesn't expect any.
